name: Georgia
disclaimer: Summarized from O.C.G.A. 48-4-5, 44-12-224 and county tax commissioner guidance. The 10 percent cap and 24-month unenforceability period are reflected in current county guidance; [VERIFY] the enacting session law and its effective date before relying on them.

tax_sale.label: Tax sale excess funds (tax commissioner / sheriff)
tax_sale.presumed_claimant: Record owner at the time of the tax sale, record holders of security deeds, and other parties with a recorded equity interest or claim, paid in order of lien priority.
tax_sale.notice_rule: Levying officer mails written notice of the excess to the record owner and lienholders within 30 days after the sale.
tax_sale.turnover_rule: After five years from the sale, unclaimed excess funds are paid to the Georgia Department of Revenue as unclaimed property.
tax_sale.redemption_note: The former owner keeps a right of redemption for 12 months after the tax sale (48-4-40). Excess funds are usually not disbursed until the redemption period has run and title has been barred; counties differ.
tax_sale.fee_cap_basis: Fees charged by third parties for assisting in recovery of excess funds may not exceed 10 percent of the excess recovered.
tax_sale.agreement_unenforceable_rule: Private agreements between claimants and third parties who locate claimants or request payment on their behalf are unenforceable for 24 months after the funds were first placed in escrow.
tax_sale.direct_payment_rule: Recovered funds must be paid directly to the claimant, not to the finder, even under a power of attorney (44-12-224 model adopted by counties).
assignment_requirements: Written agreement signed by the claimant, dated at least 24 months after the escrow date, fee stated and not more than 10 percent.
Funds payable to the claimant only; the finder invoices the claimant after payment.
Many counties require a notarized claim form, affidavit of ownership, indemnification agreement, and photo ID.
Some tax commissioners accept filings only from the claimant or a Georgia-licensed attorney; check the county before drafting.
tax_sale.claim_mechanics: Submit the county's excess funds claim form with ID, proof of ownership at time of sale, and any lien releases; conflicting claims are interpleaded into superior court.
solicitation_rules: Do not imply affiliation with the tax commissioner or sheriff.
Disclose that the owner may claim directly at no charge and that your fee is capped at 10 percent.
Georgia Fair Business Practices Act applies; the Attorney General has pursued excess funds recovery companies.
where_to_find: County tax commissioner 'Excess Funds' pages and PDF lists (Gwinnett, Fulton, Cobb, DeKalb, Chatham, Forsyth, Hall, Paulding, Athens-Clarke publish lists).
Georgia Department of Revenue unclaimed property for funds older than five years.

unclaimed_property.label: After turnover to the Department of Revenue
unclaimed_property.note: Same 10 percent cap and 24-month rule; funds paid directly to the owner.

notes: Mail first. The 24-month rule means the useful contact window opens two years after the sale and closes at five.
No autodialers or prerecorded calls; honor Do-Not-Call.
